overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email and phone outside a posted meeting, by notice-posting and notice-content defects, and by late minutes; it declined to review the correspondence-production claim and found no intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Committee members allegedly deliberated on an interim superintendent proposal by email and telephone outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This email confirms the occurrence of the prior deliberation by telephone between a quorum of the Committee's members.

allegations.summary: The July 10, 2012 meeting notice allegedly did not name the interim superintendent finalists with sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the notice for the Committee's July 10, 2012 meeting did not contain sufficient detail about a reasonably anticipated topic of discussion.

allegations.summary: Notices for the July 12 and July 24, 2012 meetings allegedly lacked specificity about executive sessions on superintendent contracts.
allegations.key_passage: The notices for the Committee's July 12, 2012 and July 24, 2012 meetings contained sufficient detail about the anticipated executive sessions regarding the employment contracts with the current Superintendent and the Interim Superintendent, respectively.

allegations.summary: The July 24, 2012 notice listed a 'Personnel Issue' executive session topic allegedly without stating the purpose.
allegations.key_passage: However, the topic, "Personnel Issue," listed on the Committee's July 24, 2012 meeting notice did not specify the executive session purpose(s) for which the Committee intended to convene in executive session.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly discussed the interim assistant superintendent contract in executive session on July 24, 2012, a topic not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing the Interim Assistant Superintendent contract during its July 24, 2012 executive session.

allegations.summary: No notice was posted for the Screening Committee's July 2, 2012 meeting or the Contract Subcommittee's July 23, 2012 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The failure to post any notice for the Screening Committee's July 2, 2012 meeting or the Contract Subcommittee's July 23, 2012 meeting violated the Open Meeting Law, and precluded the public from knowing about and attending these meetings.

allegations.summary: The Committee and Screening Committee allegedly failed to provide meeting minutes within ten days of a records request.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide meeting minutes within ten days of a request.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that correspondence not used at a meeting was not produced in time.
allegations.key_passage: Because this determination concerns only enforcement of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review the allegation that "correspondence" not used at a meeting was not timely produced, and refer the complainant to the Supervisor of Records in the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Public Records Division.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Publicly release the improper July 12, 2013 email at the Committee's next meeting
View the Attorney General's video training on the Open Meeting Law and certify in writing to the office within 30 days that all members have done so
remedy_passage: certify in writing to our office, within thirty (30) days after receiving this determination, that all of its members have done so.
